books.title: Eloquent JavaScript
books.author: Marijn Haverbeke
books.description: A thoughtful introduction to JavaScript and programming itself. It moves from language basics to higher-order functions, asynchronous code, and browser projects, with exercises at the end of each chapter.

books.title: Clean Code
books.author: Robert C. Martin
books.description: A practical guide to writing code that other people can read and maintain. It covers naming, functions, comments, error handling, and refactoring through concrete before-and-after examples.

books.title: Introduction to Algorithms
books.author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein
books.description: The standard university reference on algorithms. It covers sorting, graphs, dynamic programming, and complexity analysis with rigorous proofs, so expect a mathematical approach.

books.title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
books.author: Martin Kleppmann
books.description: Explains how modern data systems work under the hood: storage engines, replication, partitioning, transactions, and stream processing. Essential for anyone building systems that must scale.

books.title: You Don't Know JS Yet
books.author: Kyle Simpson
books.description: A deep dive into how JavaScript actually works. It explains scope, closures, objects, and the prototype system, so you stop relying on guesses about the language.

books.title: Learning React
books.author: Alex Banks, Eve Porcello
books.description: A hands-on introduction to building user interfaces with React. It covers components, hooks, state management, and data fetching, with modern patterns throughout.

books.title: Python Crash Course
books.author: Eric Matthes
books.description: A fast-paced introduction to Python for newcomers. After the fundamentals, it walks you through three real projects: a game, a data visualization, and a web application.

books.title: The Pragmatic Programmer
books.author: David Thomas, Andrew Hunt
books.description: A collection of practical advice on the craft of software development: taking responsibility, avoiding duplication, testing, automation, and thinking like a working engineer.

books.title: Grokking Algorithms
books.author: Aditya Bhargava
books.description: A friendly, illustrated introduction to algorithms. It explains searching, sorting, graphs, and dynamic programming with simple pictures instead of heavy math.

books.title: Refactoring
books.author: Martin Fowler
books.description: A catalog of small, safe code transformations that improve structure without changing behavior. It teaches when to refactor and how to do it step by step.

books.title: SQL Performance Explained
books.author: Markus Winand
books.description: Focuses on how database indexes work and how to write queries that use them well. Useful for any developer who wants faster queries without guessing.

books.title: Eloquent Ruby
books.author: Russ Olsen
books.description: Shows how to write Ruby the way experienced Rubyists do, using the language's idioms, blocks, and metaprogramming features in a natural style.
